messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 79 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.
People around you are stressed: Angela Wright, Tom Bradley, Betty Kowalski. The mood is tense.

Stephanie Morris gave Amir the honest answer: she found one party genuinely interested in the property — a regional last-mile delivery operator — but their ceiling was $255,000, well below the $300,000 floor Amir had set. No buyer materialized at the threshold he required. Amir honored his own framework: he closed the sale-inquiry path formally, thanked Stephanie, and confirmed the $350 valuation fee for payment. He called Kevin O'Brien at the bank and reactivated the $12,000 capital improvement loan; Kevin confirmed the rate and terms are still valid and scheduled a document-signing appointment for next week. Priya Sharma provided a business interruption and general liability quote — around $280 per month for combined coverage — and Amir committed to starting the policy, finally closing an insurance gap that has been open for the entire simulation. Betty Kowalski confirmed she had heard nothing from logistics or delivery operators scouting Auto Row properties, which was consistent with Stephanie's finding that the buyer demand is thinner than the thesis required.
